target_customer: Consumer apps and online businesses with product event data who wanted to predict user churn
problem: Companies lacked data scientists to model which users were about to leave and why.

founders.name: Thomson Nguyen
founders.background_notes: The YC page bio lists later roles: Visiting Partner at Y Combinator, co-founder of Saga Ventures, and founder of Nearside (acquired by Priority Financial). It gives no education or pre-2013 employers.

founders.name: Elliot Block
founders.background_notes: Listed as Founder and CTO on the YC page with no further background.

competitors.name: Mixpanel, Flurry and Amplitude
competitors.what: Product analytics firms the founder said Framed did not compete with directly

competitors.name: Gainsight, Bluenose Analytics and Totango
competitors.what: Customer success and churn analytics tools that also use behavior data

technical_complexity.rationale: Required machine learning models trained on arbitrary customer event data and a pipeline to ingest billions of events a month, hard for a two person team in 2014.

defensibility.rationale: Modeling skill was the asset, but analytics vendors could add churn prediction and the data stayed with customers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Square acquired the team in March 2016 to work on Square Capital models and shut the product down, saying it would not use the technology.

market_need_then: By December 2014 the company claimed over 600 customer companies sending about 2 billion events a month, per TechCrunch, which suggests real early usage.

branding.domain_note: Used framed.io, which now shows a 'Framed + Square' page linking to Square Capital.

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community coverage of the brand itself was found; coverage focused on the seed round and the team acquisition.

outcome_analysis: Framed Data sold churn prediction built on machine learning and raised a 2 million dollar seed in December 2014 from Google Ventures and angels, claiming hundreds of customers. In March 2016 Square hired the team into Square Capital and shut the product down at the end of the month, saying it would not use the technology. The outcome was a soft landing for the team rather than a scaled product, though no source gives the company's stated reasons or the price.
notes: YC lists the acquirer as Block, which was renamed from Square in 2021. Seed amount confirmed by TechCrunch and FinSMEs (snippet); ZoomInfo gave Google Ventures as lead, not confirmed. Education and pre-2013 employers not found for either founder.
